performance.cl_max_land_source: Airbus A320 Aircraft Characteristics Rev 46, 1 Jul 2026, section 3-5-0 p.1: threshold IAS 136 kt at MLW 66,000 kg, maximum certified flap, standard atmosphere; https://mediaassets.airbus.com/pm_38_916_916266-iujedqawwy.pdf?fileName=aca32001-jul-2026-2.pdf; existing 122.6 m^2 gross-area input supported by secondary Flugzeuginfo A320 technical data, https://www.flugzeuginfo.net/acdata_php/acdata_a320_en.php; CLmax_land recovered as 2*m*g/(rho*S*(Vref/1.23)^2), rho=1.225 kg/m^3; WV017 mass matches; planning IAS treated as sea-level CAS, rounded whole-knot speed; Airbus marks the speed for information only
performance.cl_max_to_source: Raymer, Aircraft Design: A Conceptual Approach, 5th ed., Eq. 12.21 and Table 12.2 (printed p. 415): CLmax_TO = clean 1.500 + 0.700 x flap 0.878 + leading edge 0.286 (handbook landing flap increment 0.849 = 0.9 dcl_max Sflapped/Sref cos(hinge sweep), c'/c 1.275 flap, 1.075 slat, declared control-surface spans; landing increment anchored to the published-speed landing coefficient; take-off share Raymer 60-80 % midpoint, take-off flap deflection not stated by the reference); Jane's All the World's Aircraft 2008-09, Airbus A320 entry, PDF p. 315: five-segment leading-edge slats per wing, two-segment Fowler trailing-edge flaps, slats 18/22/27 deg and flaps 10/15/20/35 deg; PDF p. 316 flap area 21.10 m2 (cross-check: 21.10/0.30 chord = 0.58 Sref flapped). Conceptual handbook estimate, not a measured CLmax: the 60-80 % take-off share is taken at its 70 % midpoint, flap and slat span and chord are the declared control-surface defaults, and the clean coefficient is the configuration's 1.5 class value.

performance.cl_max_land_source: ATR 72-600 PW127M/N Factsheet, 2020, p.2: reference speed at landing 113 KIAS, basic MLW 22,350 kg, reference wing area 61 m^2; https://www.atr-aircraft.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/Factsheets_-_ATR_72-600.pdf; CLmax_land recovered as 2*m*g/(rho*S*(Vref/1.23)^2), rho=1.225 kg/m^3; Reference speed grouped with the basic-MLW sea-level landing performance; source does not explicitly repeat its speed mass or IAS correction, so basic MLW and IAS=CAS are declared conceptual assumptions
performance.cl_max_to_source: ATR 72-600 PW127M/N Factsheet, 2020, p.2: Take-off speed (V2 min @ MTOW) 116 KCAS; weight table includes option-1 MTOW 23,000 kg and wing area 61 m^2; https://www.atr-aircraft.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/Factsheets_-_ATR_72-600.pdf; effective model CLmax_TO recovered as 2*m*g/(rho*S*(V2_min/1.2000)^2), rho=1.225 kg/m^3; The single family-wide V2 minimum line is not column-paired with the 22,800 kg basic or 23,000 kg optional MTOW; assigning it to the preset's 23,000 kg option is a declared applicability assumption. The minimum is taken as the model-selected V2; the model V2/VSR is the CS 25.107 rule max(selected 1.20, V2MIN 1.13 VSR, 1.10 VMC), so the published minimum is inverted with the part that does not depend on the control speed, 1.20: the built aircraft (computed VMC below the declared 1.13 VSR) flies the published V2, a larger control speed would raise V2 above it, and the declared fallback ratio (1.10 x 1.13 = 1.243) also flies above it. Flap configuration and whether V2 min is stall-, control- or climb-limited are unpublished. Effective lift recovery does not establish measured CLmax, VMC or a certified V2 schedule; speed reconstruction is an input check, not independent validation. Source CAS is interpreted on the ISA sea-level equivalent-density basis.

performance.cl_max_land_source: Boeing Airport Compatibility Engineering, FAA Reference Code and Approach Speeds for Boeing Aircraft, 30 Mar 2016, p.3: 787-9 approach speed 153 kt, MLW 425,000 lb; https://www.boeing.com/content/dam/boeing/v2/airports/faq/arcandapproachspeeds.pdf; 360.464 m^2 (3,880 ft^2) is the preset's own planform area, used for both this recovery and the model so Vref is reproduced (Boeing prints no wing area; an untraceable 377 m^2 OpenAP/secondary value, 4.4 % larger, was used before 2026-10-07 and made the model Vref 156.5 kt against 153 kt published); CLmax_land recovered as 2*m*g/(rho*S*(Vref/1.23)^2), rho=1.225 kg/m^3; Legacy 561,500 lb MTW / 425,000 lb MLW source matches the preset mass; area origin unverified (flugzeuginfo.net 361.0 m^2 corroborates); manufacturer planning speed treated as sea-level CAS; effective gross-area coefficient is distinct from the generic takeoff CLmax assumption
performance.cl_max_to_source: Raymer, Aircraft Design: A Conceptual Approach, 5th ed., Eq. 12.21 and Table 12.2 (printed p. 415): CLmax_TO = clean 1.500 + 0.700 x flap 0.349 + leading edge 0.242 (handbook landing flap increment 0.859 = 0.9 dcl_max Sflapped/Sref cos(hinge sweep), c'/c 1.275 flap, 1.075 slat, declared control-surface spans; landing increment anchored to the published-speed landing coefficient; take-off share Raymer 60-80 % midpoint, take-off flap deflection not stated by the reference); EASA TCDS IM.A.115 (library easa_2025_b787tcds) lists Krueger flaps (D-05-9); Jane's All the World's Aircraft 2008-09, Boeing 787 entry, PDF p. 742: inboard and outboard flaps with spoilers ahead of each, variable-camber trailing edge. Flap slot count and the Krueger span share (one inboard Krueger in four leading-edge sections) are assumptions. Conceptual handbook estimate, not a measured CLmax: the 60-80 % take-off share is taken at its 70 % midpoint, flap and slat span and chord are the declared control-surface defaults, and the clean coefficient is the configuration's 1.5 class value.
